caption:
She was born blind. Her grandmother, who raised her, is deaf and mute. There was no one in her world who could describe it to her - so she ran through it instead.

Rakshitha Raju, born in Chikmagalur, Karnataka, lost both her parents young and was raised by her grandmother in a remote village with little support for a blind child. At Ashakirana Blind School, a PE teacher spotted her running ability and took her to national meets, where guide runner Sowmya and coach Rahul Balakrishna shaped her into a competitive T11 (visually impaired) middle-distance runner. She won gold in the 1500m T11 at the 2018 Asian Para Games, gold in the 1500m and 800m at the 2019 World Para Athletics Junior Championships and gold again at the 2022 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou. At the Paris 2024 Paralympics, she became the first Indian woman to compete in the T11 1500m.
